newsitem.title: BELGIUM: No early end seen to Brussels bourse rally.
newsitem.headline: No early end seen to Brussels bourse rally.

text.p: The Brussels bourse hit new highs in active business on Monday, underpinned by the rising dollar, a strong New York close on Friday and firming European shares, and traders said they saw no early end to the rally.
"It was mainly dollar-sensitives that carried the market higher, but not exclusively," one trader said.
Traders said technical factors took a back seat as rock solid sentiment and the dollar powered the Bel-20 Belgian share index to fresh pinnacles.
"This might continue in the medium term, certainly if the dollar stays as strong as it is," another traded said.
Retailer Colruyt, drugs and chemicals giant UCB, cement firm CBR and shipper CMB were the main features of the market, each rising by more than three percent.
Traders said Colruyt, which ended 475 francs higher at 14,175 francs, was mostly a matter of the share catching up after underperforming the rest of the sector recently.

UCB, 3,000 francs higher at 93,500 francs, was a continuation of the sustained rally the stock has experienced over the last 12 months, fuelled mainly by the strong performance in the U.S. of its Zyrtec anti-allergy drug.
Traders said CBR and CMB were higher primarily because of the rampaging dollar.
CBR ended 95 francs higher at 3,410, while CMB was 75 up at 2,510 francs.

Among other stocks featured on Monday was chemical firm Solvay following its announcement after the market closed on Friday that it had raised its stake in Oy Finnish Peroxides which analysts saw as improving Solvay's position in northern Europe.
The share closed 200 francs firmer at 22,550.
The Bel-20 index ended the day 15.35 points higher at a new closing high of 2,022.14 having at one stage set a new intra-day of 2,025.39.
